payload.goal:
Add order priority and backorders to this warehouse codebase, across every layer that already exists.

Domain  - src/domain/orders.ts:
- Export type OrderPriority = "standard" | "express".
- Order gains a readonly priority field of that type. It is optional at the call site: an order placed without a priority is treated as "standard", so existing callers keep working unchanged.
- placeOrder throws OrderError when a priority is supplied and is neither "standard" nor "express".
- Export interface Backorder with readonly orderId, skuId and missing fields, where missing is a positive integer.
- WarehouseState gains a readonly backorders field keyed by order id.
- reserveOrder records a Backorder for every line whose quantity exceeds the available units, instead of throwing, and leaves the order in a status from which it can still be cancelled.
- Export listBackorders(state) returning every recorded Backorder.

Application  - src/application/warehouse-service.ts:
- The service exposes the new operations and emits a warehouse event for a recorded backorder.

Fulfillment  - src/fulfillment/planner.ts:
- Within one wave, planFulfillment lists express orders before standard ones. Its existing signature does not change.

Durability  - src/durability/journal.ts:
- HistoryAnalytics gains a backorders count derived from the events.

API  - src/api/server.ts:
- The server exposes the backorders of the current state.

Presentation  - src/presentation/tower.ts:
- The rendered SVG distinguishes express orders from standard ones.

Probe  - src/probe/g6.ts and a package script named study:g6-probe:
- Follow the shape of the existing probes: export main() returning a JSON string, and write exactly one JSON object to stdout when invoked directly, with no other output.
- Two invocations from the same commit must emit byte-identical output.

Preserve all existing behaviour and keep every existing test passing. Put new tests next to the code they cover, inside the directories the test script already scans.

scripts.test: node --test src/domain/*.test.ts src/probe/*.test.ts src/scenarios/*.test.ts src/application/*.test.ts src/presentation/*.test.ts src/api/*.test.ts src/fulfillment/*.test.ts src/durability/*.test.ts

root.title: Priority and backorders rollout
root.objective: Implement optional order priority and backorders end-to-end while preserving existing callers and tests.
expectedOutcomes: Standard callers continue to work without supplying a priority.
Short reserves produce recorded backorders rather than immediate failure where the domain now requires it.
Downstream layers can consume the new order and backorder state without contract drift.
The new probe entrypoint is stable and emits a single JSON object with no extra output.

complexitySignals.rationale: Broad end-to-end change spanning a shared domain contract and several existing consumers.

cut.rationale: The feature crosses a shared domain contract and several existing consumers, so the root groups cohesive leaves by executable seam rather than by directory.

children.title: Domain order contract
children.objective: Extend orders with optional priority and recorded backorders while preserving existing callers.
expectedOutcomes: OrderPriority is exported as standard or express.
Order gains an optional priority at the call site that defaults to standard.
placeOrder rejects invalid supplied priorities.
reserveOrder records Backorder entries and listBackorders returns them.

complexitySignals.rationale: Core contract change fans out to all downstream consumers.

children.title: Warehouse service propagation
children.objective: Expose the new service operations and backorder event while keeping simulation and service tests green.
expectedOutcomes: The service exposes the new order and backorder operations required by the domain change.
A recorded backorder produces a warehouse event.
Simulation coverage still compiles and exercises the updated service surface.

complexitySignals.rationale: Service behavior must stay aligned with domain rules and the existing simulator-facing surface.

children.title: Fulfillment wave ordering
children.objective: Keep the planner signature unchanged while ordering express work ahead of standard work within a wave.
expectedOutcomes: One-wave planning places express orders before standard orders.
Existing planner callers keep the same signature and behavior outside the new ordering rule.
Planner tests cover mixed-priority waves.

complexitySignals.rationale: Small planner change, but it must preserve the existing entrypoint and ordering semantics.

children.title: Durability analytics update
children.objective: Derive the new backorders count from journaled events.
expectedOutcomes: HistoryAnalytics includes a backorders count derived from the event history.
Journal tests cover the new derived metric without changing unrelated history calculations.

complexitySignals.rationale: Derived-state update with event-history coupling and regression coverage needs.

children.title: API state exposure
children.objective: Expose the current state's backorders through the server surface.
expectedOutcomes: The server response includes backorders from the current state.
Server tests verify the new field without regressing the existing API shape.

complexitySignals.rationale: Public response shape change with direct consumer-visible regression risk.

children.title: Tower priority rendering
children.objective: Render express and standard orders distinctly in the SVG output.
expectedOutcomes: Express orders are visually distinguishable from standard orders in the rendered tower SVG.
Tower tests cover both priority states and preserve existing rendering expectations.

complexitySignals.rationale: Mostly local rendering work, but it must align with the shared priority contract.

children.title: G6 probe and script
children.objective: Add the new probe entrypoint and script with deterministic single-JSON stdout behavior.
expectedOutcomes: src/probe/g6.ts exports main() returning a JSON string.
Direct invocation writes exactly one JSON object to stdout and nothing else.
Two runs from the same commit produce byte-identical output.
package.json exposes the study:g6-probe script.

complexitySignals.rationale: New entrypoint plus reproducibility requirements and a dedicated test surface.
